Article Title: SP to field third candidate in UP Rajya Sabha polls? How move would trigger contest with BJP
Article Text:
The SP has so far announced two candidates, both of whom are assured of win

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party (SP) MP Virendra Singh on Friday announced that the party will field a third candidate in the upcoming Rajya Sabha elections in Uttar Pradesh, despite only two SP candidates being assured of victory.If the SP fields a third candidate, it would set up a contest with the ruling BJP for one seat. Seven BJP candidates are assured of victory. Polling for 10 vacant Rajya Sabha seats from the state is scheduled for October 16.“We will decide our third candidate today and the nomination will be filed by October 5,” Singh told PTI.The Chandauli MP further remarked that the SP would adopt the “same strategy” the BJP used to secure the election of its candidates in the previous Rajya Sabha polls.“We will get all three of our candidates elected through the same route by which the BJP had got its candidates elected in the last Rajya Sabha elections,” Singh added.He also claimed that several BJP MLAs seeking SP tickets for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections were in touch with the Akhilesh Yadav-led party.Singh’s remarks came a day after Akhilesh Yadav declined to confirm whether the SP would field a third candidate, suggesting that the BJP could put up “nine or even 10 candidates.”The SP on September 30 nominated veteran party leader and Akhilesh Yadav’s uncle, Ram Gopal Yadav, and Reliance Industries executive Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani for the elections. Both subsequently filed their nomination papers in Lucknow.The number of first-preference votes required to win a Rajya Sabha seat in Uttar Pradesh depends on the number of vacancies and the number of MLAs eligible to vote. With 10 seats up for election this time, the winning benchmark is likely to be around 37 first-preference votes.The BJP currently has 255 MLAs in the 403-member Uttar Pradesh assembly, while its NDA allies have another 33, taking the alliance’s combined strength to 288.The SP has 101 MLAs. Three legislators who defected to the BJP are currently unattached, while rebel MLA Puja Pal remains listed with the SP despite having joined the BJP. The Congress, an SP ally, has two MLAs.In the 2024 Rajya Sabha elections in Uttar Pradesh, the BJP won all eight seats it contested, while two of the SP’s three nominees were elected. The SP’s third candidate, Alok Ranjan, lost.Rajya Sabha elections are conducted through proportional representation using the single transferable vote system. Under this system, surplus votes received by winning candidates can be transferred to other candidates based on voters’ subsequent preferences.As a result, if more than 10 candidates enter the fray, the contest could hinge on the distribution and transfer of votes, making electoral arithmetic and strategy crucial.
Article Summary: The sp has so far announced two candidates, both of whom are assured of win. Polling for 10 vacant rajya sabha seats from the state is scheduled for october 16. If the sp fields a third candidate, it would set up a contest with the ruling bjp for one seat.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay plays bus conductor, hands out tickets after expanding free travel scheme
Article Text:
CM Vijay personally handed out free tickets to women.

What is Vettri Payanam scheme?

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Friday launched the expanded 'Vettri Payanam Thittam', extending free bus travel to more categories of services for women and transgender people across the state.Marking the launch on Gandhi Jayanti, Vijay travelled by bus in Chennai, interacted with passengers and personally handed out free tickets to women.In a light-hearted moment, college students travelling on the bus were also seen sharing Dairy Milk chocolates with the chief minister.The expanded scheme is expected to benefit around 84.32 lakh women every day. Beneficiaries can travel free of cost on 12,695 buses operated by seven state transport corporations, including services in the express and deluxe categories.There is no income ceiling to avail the scheme and no limit on the number of trips a beneficiary can make in a day, the state government said.The scheme, whose name is derived from the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), meaning “victorious journey”, was earlier limited to certain categories of buses. The expanded facility now covers express, deluxe, mofussil ordinary and certain Ghat-area services.Earlier, transport minister A Vijay Tamilan Parthiban said the scheme aims to support the education, employment, livelihoods and economic empowerment of women and transgender people by ensuring that transportation costs do not become a barrier to their progress.He said the initiative was also aimed at promoting equality, adding that there should be no distinction in travel rights.Parthiban described the scheme as a “social revolution” that would help women become more independent, step out of their homes and contribute to the state’s growth."The launch is also meant to honour the principles of social justice and women's empowerment, to facilitate their participation in the economy and society, ensuring that transportation costs do not hinder their access to education, employment, or healthcare," the minister added.
Article Summary: The expanded scheme is expected to benefit around 84.32 lakh women every day. Beneficiaries can travel free of cost on 12,695 buses operated by seven state transport corporations. No income ceiling to avail the scheme and no limit on the number of trips a beneficiary can make in a day.

Article Title: Captain Smit Machchhar: A steady hand, in and out of the cockpit
Article Text:
Captain Smit Machchhar with his wife Sonal

.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Long before he was the captain who held a cockpit together despite stab wounds, Capt Smit Machchhar was the pilot who interacted with loaders, engineers, ground staff, catering people, all with equal respect.“Smit is the most calm, composed and down-to-earth person you could ever meet,” said Capt Dharav Gosalia, a friend since his flying school days.On Wednesday, that steadiness was tested at altitude. flydubai flight FZ1073 was carrying 174 people from Dubai to Tel Aviv when, according to Israeli officials, Machchhar’s co-pilot stabbed him and tried to crash the aircraft. The jet reportedly dropped nearly 14,000 feet in under 30 seconds. Seriously wounded, Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door, letting passengers and crew overpower the attacker. The plane landed in Saudi Arabia.Those who know Machchhar, 39, are not surprised by how he behaved. What shocks them is that it was ever required. “He is one of the calmest and most fun guys possible,” said a friend, a B737 pilot who requested anonymity. “Maybe it is his upbringing. He is always in fun mode, but he is family-oriented too.”Machchhar earned his commercial pilot licence at Mainland Aviation College in New Zealand in the late 2000s, where he became the classmates’ go-to person for hard subjects. “Anyone with a problem in air navigation, aircraft technical or any subject went to him,” the pilot said. “Becoming a line trainer at flydubai was the best thing that could have happened to him.”The instinct to help was visible earlier, too. At M D Bhatia School, where he passed Class 10 in 2003, school friend Bhavin Jethva remembers him as “straightforward, bindass”. “He didn’t like to lie,” Jethva said. “He was never fake and he couldn’t pretend.” Amit Soni, a childhood friend who played cricket with him, called him cheerful and lively.At Swastik Heights in Mumbai’s Tilak Nagar, where Machchhar lived until about 2022, neighbour Laxmikanth Joshi remembers practical kindnesses. After returning from Kenya, Joshi realised he had bought too little coffee to share with friends. Machchhar arranged for a pilot colleague to bring back more. Joshi also remembers Machchhar going straight to the hospital after landing in India when his father underwent bypass surgery about six months ago. He stayed through the treatment. Then there were the Independence Day and Republic Day celebrations. He recalls Capt Machchhar taught them to tie the rope into a knot just right. “One pull and the flag unfurled,” recalled Joshi.Akshay Joshi, his immediate neighbour, recalls tense moments at his place when his parents learned about the attack. Late in the evening, though, Machchhar’s parents informed the society’s WhatsApp group that their son was recovering.Capt Machchhar moved to Dubai around 2022 after leaving SpiceJet, and flies the Boeing 737 as a captain and line trainer at flydubai. He and his wife, Sonal, have two children: Krishay, 2, and Ziva, 9.Friends and colleagues tried to reconstruct the sequence. A B737 commander said the co-pilot would most likely have used the ‘crash axe’, which is carried on the flight deck for use during emergencies, such as cutting through panels and debris, or the cockpit window to exit the aircraft after an accident. “At the Dubai airport, even shoes and belts are removed at security,” he said. “There’s no way the co-pilot could have got onboard with a pocket knife. ”Another colleague said the co-pilot “apparently stood up and hit Machchhar on the side of the head”. This colleague added that the captain was also struck in the chest, before he regained control after the dive. A third pilot said Machchhar appeared to have squawked ‘7500’, the hijack transponder code. A B737 commander also pointed to a gap: “We have SOPs for a hijack scenario, but not for a cockpit where the aggressor is inside.” He noted that Capt Machchhar’s bravery boils down to two acts: first, he managed to get the aircraft straight and level after that precarious dive, despite being attacked; second, though he had lost a lot of blood, he managed to open the cockpit door before he passed out.At M D Bhatia School, former classmates have been posting prayers for his recovery on their WhatsApp group. “We are proud of him,” Jethva said.
Article Summary: Captain smit machchhar was stabbed by his co-pilot. He managed to open the cockpit door, letting passengers and crew overpower the attacker. The jet reportedly dropped nearly 14,000 feet in under 30 seconds. Those who know him are not surprised by how he behaved.

Article Title: Karnataka BJP leader booked over alleged bid to delete names of 198 'Muslim voters'
Article Text:
BLO lodges FIR against BJP leader over alleged bid to delete 198 voter names during SIR

NEW DELHI: An FIR has been registered against Karnataka BJP leader Ravi Patil and others for allegedly attempting to get the names of 198 Muslim voters deleted from the electoral roll in Belagavi district through Form-7 applications during the ongoing SIR process, police said on Friday, as cited by news agency PTI.Police said the case was registered at Belagavi Market police station on September 30 based on a complaint by Meerasab Sanadi, a Booth Level Agent for Ward No. 12 in the Belagavi North Assembly constituency.At least two FIRs have so far been registered over alleged “SIR irregularities”, including one in Mysuru against local BJP leaders and others, with the complainant alleging a “conspiracy” to get his, his family's and other members of the “Muslim community's votes deleted during the SIR process and thereby, hurting the religious sentiments of the community and creating disturbance in society”.The FIR has been registered under Sections 318(4) (cheating), 336(3) (forgery), 336(4) (forgery intended to harm reputation), 353 (statements conducing to public mischief), 61(2) (criminal conspiracy), 3(5) (common intention), 192 (wantonly giving provocation with intent to cause a riot) and 190 (liability of members of an unlawful assembly for offences committed in pursuit of its common object) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.Police said further investigation is underway.According to the FIR, the complainant said he was assisting the Booth Level Officer (BLO) in the Election Commission’s ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and helping verify voter details.He alleged that on September 22, around 2.30 pm, the accused, including Patil, Shankar Beerappa Naik and Pashant Deepak Mundinmani, along with 20 to 25 others, allegedly assembled with the intention of targeting voters and conspired to have their names removed from the electoral roll.The accused allegedly prepared forged documents and submitted them to the BLO, falsely claiming that they were genuine documents issued by the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO), the complainant alleged. He further alleged that the Form-7 applications submitted with the purportedly fake documents included the names of 198 voters, including him and his family members."They allegedly exerted pressure on the BLO and made another person speak over the phone claiming to be the ERO and obtained his signature, thereby cheating the complainant and the voters," the FIR said.Form 7 is the prescribed application form for filing an objection to the proposed inclusion or deletion of a name from the existing electoral roll.In another such case in Bidar, 40-year-old businessman and Bhalki voter Mohammed Ateeq Ahmed alleged in his complaint that 3,244 voters, including him, were falsely shown as “shifted/absent” through Form 7 applications during the SIR of electoral rolls.According to the FIR, Ahmed alleged that the applications were submitted without obtaining authenticated documents from the affected voters and that their signatures were forged with the intention of getting their names deleted from the electoral roll.Following his complaint, police registered an FIR on October 1, naming 32 people as accused in connection with the alleged irregularities.Karnataka chief minister D K Shivakumar, along with his Cabinet colleagues and MLAs, staged a sit-in outside the office of Chief Electoral Officer V Anbukkumar on Thursday, demanding registration of an FIR over alleged “electoral fraud” during the ongoing SIR of electoral rolls.
Article Summary: Blo lodges fir against bjp leader over alleged bid to delete 198 voter names during sir process. At least two firs have so far been registered over alleged “sir irregularities” in karnataka. Complainant alleges a “conspiracy’ to get his, his family's and other members of the “muslim community's votes deleted during the sir process”

NEW DELHI: Entry and exit at 12 Delhi Metro stations will remain closed until further notice amid heightened security arrangements in New Delhi over a proposed protest at Jantar Mantar against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.However, interchange facilities will remain available at Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House, New Delhi and Central Secretariat stations.These 12 metro stations to remain closed.Delhi Police has denied permission for the proposed protest at Jantar Mantar on Gandhi Jayanti and deployed additional security personnel in and around New Delhi, officials told news agency PTI.The protest, called by the All India Students' Association (AISA), Rajya Sabha MP Manoj Jha and Supreme Court lawyer Prashant Bhushan, is scheduled to begin at 11 am on Friday.Police sources said around 3,000 to 4,000 people were expected to attend the gathering, prompting heightened security arrangements in the area.Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) personnel have been deployed alongside Delhi Police teams at Jantar Mantar and other key points in New Delhi district.Barricades have been put up, while additional personnel have been positioned at entry and exit points and other sensitive locations to regulate movement and prevent any unauthorised gathering, the sources said.The organisers are seeking the resignation or impeachment of Gyanesh Kumar, alleging irregularities in electoral rolls and the conduct of elections.They have also raised concerns over the Election Commission's handling of electoral rolls and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, claiming that it raises questions over the protection of citizens' voting rights.The proposed protest comes amid demonstrations by opposition parties, student groups and civil society activists in Delhi over the functioning of the poll panel and the SIR exercise.

Article Title: Of 97 left out in Goa, 88 are back, 3 others are Portuguese citizens: EC
Article Text:
Goans born before 1961 in former Portuguese territories, as well as their kids and grandchildren, can apply for a Portuguese passport based on a citizen card issued by the Portuguese authorities after verifying their birth/descent documents.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The office of the Goa chief electoral officer on Thursday said 88 of the 97 voters in the state whose names could not be included in the roll due to an alleged ECINet issue have been added back after their duly filled Form 6 was accepted. However, he also revealed that three of these 97 electors are Portuguese passport holders while six others were electors currently based outside India."In respect of voters who are currently residing outside India, officials are making efforts to establish and maintain contact with them for necessary action," the CEO said while sharing the status report on the 97 cases on X.Section 9 of the Constitution disallows dual citizenship. Goans born before 1961 in former Portuguese territories, as well as their kids and grandchildren, can apply for a Portuguese passport based on a citizen card issued by the Portuguese authorities after verifying their birth/descent documents. Portugal recognises dual citizenship; however, since dual citizenship is not allowed in India, anybody who acquires a foreign passport must surrender his Indian passport.As per Sec 9 of the Citizenship Act, 1955, a person's Indian citizenship automatically ceases upon acquiring foreign citizenship.Thus, three of the Portuguese passport holders in Goa may be classified as non-citizens, making them ineligible to be enrolled as Indian electors, said a source.Incidentally, Portuguese passport holders form 3% of the cohort of 97 electors for which the Goa CEO had repeatedly written to the EC after the ERO could not add them back via ERONet, leading the ECs to also raise questions on why access for such changes was 'centralised' and not available to the field officers. The issue was further amplified by the opposition parties after The Indian Express reported on the alleged internal notes of the election commissioners in this regard.EC sources on Thursday said the due diligence by the ERO the second time around may have served the purpose of SIR, as it is aimed at eliminating ineligible persons from the voters' list. Also, the fact that the issue was detected at the ERO level proves that the absolute right to add or delete a voter, based on verification, remains with the field officers, an EC officer told TOI.
Article Summary: 88 of the 97 voters in the state whose names could not be included in the roll due to an alleged ecinet issue have been added back. Three of these 97 electors are portuguese passport holders while six others were electors currently based outside india.

Article Title: Delhi riots case: High court rejects bail pleas Of Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam
Article Text:
Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam denied bail by high court

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court has refused to grant bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the UAPA case related to the 2020 Delhi riots.Senior Advocate Trideep Pais, appearing for Umar Khalid, submitted that there had been three “small changes in circumstances” since the earlier proceedings. He also referred the court to a Supreme Court judgment in support of his submissions.Pais pointed out that charges have not yet been framed in the case and, consequently, prosecution witnesses are yet to be examined. The court also noted that the charges were yet to be framed.Pais further submitted that a Special Leave Petition (SLP) is pending before the Supreme Court and that the trial court has indicated it would await the Supreme Court’s order. He then continued his submissions by referring to the Supreme Court judgment.Khalid and Imam had approached the Delhi High Court earlier this year after their bail applications were dismissed by the trial court for the third time on July 4. Imam was arrested in the case on August 25, 2020, while Khalid was arrested on September 13, 2020.The Delhi Police has opposed their bail pleas in the high court, asserting that the two were “masterminds” of the riots, PTI reported.The police argued that they could not seek bail on parity with other co-accused, stating that the Supreme Court had earlier categorised them as being part of the “command authority” and held that their “risk profiles” justified “continuing detention”.The police also argued that the present bail pleas were in the teeth of the Supreme Court’s January 5 order, which directed them to seek release only after the examination of protected witnesses was completed or after one year, whichever was earlier.On July 4, the trial court rejected Khalid’s bail application, saying it had “no option but to follow” the Supreme Court’s January 5 order and could therefore neither entertain the plea nor grant him relief.On September 2, 2025, a Delhi High Court division bench denied bail to Khalid and Imam. The Supreme Court upheld the verdict on January 5 but granted relief to co-accused Gulfisha Fatima, Meeran Haider, Shifa Ur Rehman, Mohammad Saleem Khan and Shadab Ahmad.A bench of Justice Aravind Kumar and Justice NV Anjaria had observed that there was a prima facie case against Khalid and Imam under the UAPA.On May 22, the Supreme Court granted six months’ interim bail to co-accused Abdul Khalid Saifi and Tasleem Ahmad, while referring to a larger bench the issue of prolonged incarceration of undertrials under the UAPA due to the stringent conditions for granting bail.
Article Summary: Umar khalid, sharjeel imam denied bail by high court in uapa case related to 2020 delhi riots. Delhi police has opposed their bail pleas in the high court, asserting that the two were ‘masterminds’ of the riots.

NEW DELHI: Aam Aadmi Party leader Atishi and All India Students’ Association (AISA) national president Neha Bora were detained at Jantar Mantar on Friday as protests over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls intensified, with the number of people detained crossing 700.Atishi's X post reads, “Modi Ji: We haven't come here to fear your police. To save the right to vote, we will keep fighting ✊🏼”Earlier today, AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj and party MLA Sanjeev Jha were detained by Delhi Police on Friday after they reached Jantar Mantar to join a protest against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.“Despite the peaceful protest, Delhi Police arrested MLA Sanjeev Jha ji and Saurabh. But the movement will continue!," reads offical AAP X post.Bharadwaj, on X, later informed that more than 500 people had reached Jantar Mantar ahead of the scheduled protest. "GenZ rocks," he wrote.According to TOI sources, mobile internet services have been disrupted in the Jantar Mantar area, with some users receiving a message stating that internet services have been suspended in the area “as per government instructions” until further notice.Massive protests are planned in Delhi and Mumbai today, with the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) set to launch its nationwide agitation from Mumbai’s Shivaji Park.The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), All India Students’ Association (AISA), National Students’ Union of India (NSUI) and Indian Youth Congress (IYC) have announced a separate demonstration at Jantar Mantar in Delhi.“Appointment of CEC should be transparent; there should be involvement of civil society,” Dipke said in Mumbai.The CJP and opposition parties have criticised Kumar over the SIR of electoral rolls and demanded his resignation.Their criticism intensified after it emerged that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded objections on at least 14 occasions over 10 months to certain decisions and orders, some of which they said were issued without their knowledge.The Election Commission later clarified that the three-member commission had taken all decisions, including those relating to the SIR, unanimouslyIn a new video, Dipke was seen posing with an auto driver as the two urged commuters and residents to gather at the protest venue. "Chala chala shivaji park.. shivaji park… shivaji park…," the caption reads.The auto driver in the video can be heard saying 'Shivaji Park 4 baje'.Police in both Delhi and Mumbai have denied permission for the proposed protests. In Delhi, prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) are in force across the New Delhi district, restricting public meetings or assemblies of five or more people, processions, demonstrations, picketing and dharnas without prior written permission.Delhi DCP said that the restrictions have been imposed to ensure public safety, maintain public order and facilitate smooth traffic movement.In Mumbai, police have also denied permission for the proposed gathering at Shivaji Park. Police said they were not authorised to permit such a gathering there in view of a 2013 Bombay High Court order and described the area as a silence zone.Meanwhile, the Delhi Metro has also closed entry and exit at 11 stations, including Rajiv Chowk, Central Secretariat, Janpath, Patel Chowk, Seva Teerth, Mandi House, Lok Kalyan Marg, INA, Chawri Bazar, Ramakrishna Ashram Marg and New Delhi, until further notice.
Article Summary: Massive protest erupts in two major cities against cec gyanesh kumar. Atishi and all india students’ association (aisa) national president neha bora detained at jantar mantar. Police deny permission for the proposed gathering at shivaji park.

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission has directed state poll officials to launch a special drive to immediately enrol “left-out” and new voters in areas where the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) has been completed. The move comes amid allegations by the opposition parties that the electoral roll revision exercise disenfranchised crores of eligible citizens.The instructions were conveyed in an official communication issued on Thursday, following a virtual meeting with state chief electoral officers (CEOs), as cited by PTI.The drive aims to re-enrol eligible voters who were omitted or deleted during the intensive revision, while also registering first-time and “young voters”.The Commission stressed that voter registration is an ongoing process and that no eligible citizen should be disenfranchised for not being included during the SIR enumeration.Booth Level Officers (BLOs) have been instructed to cross-check the current electoral rolls with pre-SIR lists to identify electors whose names were included earlier but dropped from the final roll.BLOs will conduct house-to-house verification of all identified missing electors.Each officer will be tasked with covering 20 to 25 electors a week, with the verification drive targeted for completion within a month.BLOs will also collect Form 6 applications on the spot from newly eligible young electors and genuine left-out voters. The lists will subsequently be shared directly with Booth Level Agents (BLAs) of recognised political parties to ensure transparency.The move follows a September 26 meeting of the full Commission, comprising Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi. After the meeting, the poll panel said the declaration attached to Form 6 was meant “specifically for SIR” and that “for non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules (the Registration of Electors Rules 1960) will be used.”The Election Commission has withdrawn the additional SIR-related declaration attached to Form 6 in states where the electoral roll revision exercise has been completed.The declaration has been removed from the ECINET app and portal, as well as the respective Chief Electoral Officer portals. New applicants in these states will now only have to submit the regular statutory Form 6 for voter enrolment.In states and Union territories where the SIR exercise is still underway, the additional declaration remains available on the ECINET portal. Under the declaration, new applicants are required to provide details linking themselves, their parents or grandparents to electoral rolls prepared during an earlier SIR.

Opposition parties allege that the electoral roll revision exercise disenfranchised crores of eligible citizens. The drive aims to re-enrol eligible voters who were omitted or deleted during the intensive revision.

Article Title: Chita Andolan is back: Why are Madhya Pradesh's Panna villagers protesting against Ken-Betwa project
Article Text:
MP dam project: Protesters brave rain and waterlogging for 20th day

What is happening in Madhya Pradesh's Panna?

Several women and other protesters had fallen ill after staying in water and rain for several days, with some suffering from wounds on their feet and other skin-related problems. (ANI photo)

So why are the protesters back?

For thousands of tribal families living in the path of the project, it has become a battle over land, forests, livelihoods and identity.

Affected families have staged some of the country's most striking demonstrations, standing waist-deep in river water, laying beside symbolic funeral pyres and even climbed symbolic gallows.

'Ken-Betwa River Linking Project' is India's first river-linking initiative aimed to transform the drought-prone Bundelkhand region through irrigation, drinking water supply and power generation.

What is the project aiming to accomplish?

Poll Vote & Share your view How satisfied are you with the government response to the recent protests in Panna? Very satisfied Not satisfied 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Remember the unnerving visuals from Chita Andolan in Madhya Pradesh? Displaced Tribals sleeping on pyres, standing in water for their compensation. The unique protest is back and in its 20th day with agitators battling rain, waterlogging, lathicharge and general apathy by the authorities.Activist Amit Bhatnagar, Jai Kisan Sangathan leader, who has been on a hunger strike for the past four days, was arrested on Wednesday as protesters demonstrated chita, jal, sooli, mitti, bhook (pyre, water, gallows, soil, hunger) other forms of satyagraha.Bhatnagar accused the Panna administration of suppressing the agitation by lathicharging protesters, including women.Speaking to TOI before his arrest, Bhatnagar said, "For the past three days, the police have been bringing along people dressed in plain clothes, who misbehaved with women, entered their homes and even took away people’s phones which have still not been returned. When we approach the police, they ask who took the phones. How are people supposed to identify every face and find out who took them?""There is an atmosphere of fear in the villages. If we say anything, they start resorting to lathi-charge and filing false cases against the protesters," he added.“I am courting arrest because democracy is being murdered. Are we not even allowed to protest peacefully? We are putting ourselves through hardship to raise our concerns, but instead of listening to us, they have cut off the electricity and water. Even the British never did this. ”The latest protest follows a 15-day agitation in July, led largely by tribal women, after which the administration had assured protesters that eligible and genuinely displaced families would be transparently included in compensation and rehabilitation lists.However, the protesters claimed that they did not get the promised compensation. Also, their houses were now inundated, with two to three feet of water entering homes in several villages which now stand waterlogged including Mandalia, Tapariya and Kuwarpur."The families whose houses have been submerged are so poor that they have been forced to continue living there, or put up one makeshift shelter next to another, and then another. Earlier, the water would rise by half a foot at a time. But this time there was heavy rain on the 26th and 27th of September, followed by a 24-hour red alert, leaving them with no time to move. The villages turned into islands,” said Bhatnagar.The protesters claim that the compensation process remains incomplete, with several families receiving only Rs 5 lakh despite the government announcing a Rs 12.5-lakh package.They are also opposing the compensation conditions, which makes several tribals ineligible for relief.“The cut-off date under Section 11 has been set as 2018, which means people who are now 25-26 years old have received nothing. Those who are older are getting only Rs 5 lakh. What are families with eight or 10 children supposed to do?" asked Bhatnagar, adding that they were not against development projects, but that this development should not come at the cost of the rights of tribals.Bhatnagar pointed to Section 38 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, which he said raised concerns about any displacement or submergence taking place before compensation and rehabilitation obligations had been fulfilled.“Villages and homes are now submerged. Houses have started collapsing and water has entered them. Yet, Section 38 of the 2013 law says that compensation for an irrigation project should be paid six months before submergence. If the houses were submerged two months ago, compensation should have been paid eight months earlier,” he said.The authorities, on the other hand, claim that they have been conducting fresh surveys and distributing compensation to affected families. TOI reached out to Chhatarpur district magistrate and is still awaiting a response from the administration.The Majhgawan dam project aims to transfer surplus water from Ken river to Betwa through the Daudhan Dam, a network of tunnels and a 221-km canal. It is supposed to address water shortages in drought-prone Bundelkhand region that spans across Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.The project traces back to a plan introduced in 1980 and cleared in 2021 to connect the rivers. Prime Minister Narendra Modi laid its foundation stone in December 2024.The project is expected to improve agricultural output, curb migration and strengthen groundwater recharge through the revival of traditional Chandela-era ponds.
Article Summary: Mp dam project: protesters brave rain and waterlogging for 20th day. Affected families have staged some of the country's most striking demonstrations. Several women and other protesters had fallen ill after staying in water and rain for several days. The majhgawan dam project aims to transfer surplus water from ken river to betwa.

Article Title: How India's classrooms are coping in the age of instant gratification & low attention spans
Article Text:
Representative image.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Classrooms in parts of India are grappling with an underlying problem that no curriculum revision can easily fix. Students raised on on-demand food delivery, constant social media reels and instant AI answers are finding it harder to sustain attention, tolerate boredom, or work toward rewards that don't arrive at once.Teachers, as a result, are increasingly engaging a generation that is much less attentive than before. A recent nationwide survey by the National Council of CBSE Schools found that almost 70% of teachers across the country have observed a sharp decline in their students' focus and classroom attention.The survey, which covered around 6.3 lakh respondents -- teachers, under 18 students and their parents -- also found that 74% of students spend more than two hours a day on screen for non-academic purposes. And teachers reported rising anxiety, irritability and reduced face-to-face interaction among children.Parmeshwar Dattarao Bhurke, a teacher, says the trend is evident in everyday classroom experiences. "Many children no longer have the focus needed to sit through an hour-long lesson or read a passage without their minds wandering," he said. This has prompted many teachers to experiment with newer learning methods, he added."Earlier, one student could read a chapter aloud while the rest of the class listened. That no longer works. .. The idea now is to keep their minds actively engaged through the session."Priya, another middle school teacher, says she has noticed a decline in students' retention levels. "Even when children appear to be listening, their minds are elsewhere. They are also less willing to struggle through any difficult task. This affects their performance in school as well as their behaviour, as they become averse to any kind of challenges or discomfort."For 15-year-old student Chinmayee Sonna, the shift is visible in the way her classmates now study. "Instead of sitting with textbooks or working through ideas, many of my classmates look for the easier option, whether that is AI-generated summaries or explainer videos. They are able to retain less through this method but it helps revise quickly and saves time," she said.Psychologists say such habits reflect a behavioural shift driven by constant access to instant rewards. "They trigger dopamine, giving us a brief rush of joy that reinforces the behaviour and makes us want to repeat it. This is different from the real-life feats, where satisfaction comes only after much effort and patience," Rashi Bhatnagar, a psychologist, said.It is these consequences that extend into the classroom. "When rewards come with almost no effort, the brain begins to prefer them. Like an unused muscle, our ability to wait, tolerate boredom and sustain attention gradually weakens, leaving us restless when tasks demand patience," Bhatnagar said.This is why there is a downside to schools trying to make every lesson entertaining, she adds. "Education cannot always provide instant pleasure if it is to encourage deep thinking. Schools need to consciously create opportunities for children to reflect and generate new ideas."The habit of expecting immediate outcomes also affects resilience. "Because children have not developed the ability to wait for results, many give up too quickly. We need to teach them not to quit at the first sign of difficulty," Bhatnagar said.Psychiatrist Nisha Singla, talking about the digital ecosystem, says it is deliberately designed to reinforce instant gratification. "Social media apps, notifications and quick commerce applications are addictive and the brain begins to crave them. Reading or learning something new also gives us a sense of achievement, but the reward is delayed. That is where all the difference lies."Rebuilding patience, she says, begins with allowing children to slow down. "We need to let them get bored... There is a tendency to fill every moment of their day with something or the other, but boredom is equally important. Parents and schools should consciously encourage delayed gratification."Another challenge to consider in adapting classrooms is large class sizes and poor teacher-student ratios. "This leaves little room for us to nurture each child's curiosity and individual learning needs. At the same time, schools remain under pressure to deliver high marks and pass percentages, leaving us focused on examination outcomes rather than redesigning learning around children's changing needs," Priya said.As educators wait for the national mental health and well-being policy for schools, they say it should help students find meaning in a learning process whose greatest rewards cannot be a sprint and a quick fix.
Article Summary: Survey by national council of cbse schools found that almost 70% of teachers have observed a sharp decline in their students' focus and classroom attention. 74% of students spend more than two hours a day on screen for non-academic purposes. Teachers reported rising anxiety, irritability and reduced face-to-face interaction among children.

Article Title: No uniform explanation for collegium decisions on compassionate transfers
Article Text:
The five-member collegium on Sept 28 recommended the repatriation of Justice T Vinod Kumar from Madras HC to his parent HC in Telangana 'in view of his ensuing retirement on Nov 16'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court collegium's decisions to transfer judges from one HC to another are explained as being meant "for the better administration of justice". But the standard reasoning does not translate into a uniform explanation, with the collegium showing unusual compassion in approving requests from some for transfer or repatriation due to difficult family situations or health issues, while maintaining aloofness from others.There are many judges in HCs who have expressed resentment at the absence of any procedure or norm for transfer of HC judges. A member of the collegium, who will go on to become CJI, has mooted framing a transparent transfer policy. He told TOI that a judge under consideration for transfer should be warned first to mend his ways and be kept under watch for some time. Only when he does not improve should he be transferred, he said.The five-member collegium on Sept 28 recommended the repatriation of Justice T Vinod Kumar from Madras HC to his parent HC in Telangana "in view of his ensuing retirement on Nov 16". Justice Kumar was transferred from Telangana HC to Madras HC in May last year by the SC collegium headed by then CJI BR Gavai.In May last year, a complaint had reached the SC alleging that Justice Kumar, heading a division bench, had kept more than 50 judgments reserved.Sitting as a single judge, he had reserved verdicts in over 170 cases since 2020. If Justice Kumar's imminent retirement was a ground for his repatriation, no such consideration was shown to Justice D Nagarjun, who was transferred from Telangana HC to Madras HC. Justice Nagarjun, a career judicial officer who was elevated as an HC judge in March 2022, was transferred to Madras HC in April 2023.As he was due to retire on Aug 14, 2024, he sent a request to the CJI on July 25, 2024, for repatriation to his parent HC in Telangana, but the collegium remained aloof to the request and allowed him to retire in Madras HC.A Punjab and Haryana HC judge represented against his transfer to another HC, citing his wife's serious illness and disability of his child. But that evoked no compassion with the collegium, which remained firm on his transfer.Justice D V Ramana, who was only 13 years old when his railway gangman father died in an accident, rose from humble backgrounds to become a judge of Andhra Pradesh HC in Aug 2022. He was transferred to Madhya Pradesh HC in Nov 2023. On his retirement in May last year, he gave vent to his frustration. He said he was asked for options and chose Karnataka HC to enable better treatment for his wife, who had a neurological disorder. But that was not heeded. He again requested a transfer to Karnataka to help his wife get treated at Nimhans but that was neither considered nor rejected.
Article Summary: The five-member collegium on sept 28 recommended the repatriation of justice t vinod kumar from madras hc to his parent hc in telangana. Justice kumar's imminent retirement was a ground for his repatriation, but no such consideration was shown to justice d nagarjun.

Article Title: Government mandates full body scanners at 8 airports; no timeline yet, trials on
Article Text:
(Representative image): The scanners installed for trials are integrated to door-frame metal detectors and the results of the former are matched with what the latter detects during passenger checks.

NEW DELHI: Indian airports may finally see full body scanners (FBS) after several missed deadlines in the past few years due to changing regulatory requirements. Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS) DG Rajesh Nirwan said on Thursday that FBS have been mandated for eight airports and trials are on at Bengaluru and Kochi. Kochi is not among the airports where the same has been mandated. Hyderabad and Delhi are in that list, and "site acceptance" is under way there.The scanners installed for trials are integrated to door-frame metal detectors and the results of the former are matched with what the latter detects during passenger checks. BCAS is collecting the data and the algorithms will be refined based on the outcome.Dismissing privacy concerns, Nirwan said scanners are being made "image agnostic" as they will just be a model of a person.
Article Summary: Indian airports may finally see full body scanners (fbs) after several missed deadlines in the past few years due to changing regulatory requirements. Fbs have been mandated for eight airports and trials are on at bengaluru and kochi. The scanners installed for trials are integrated to door-frame metal detectors and the results of the former are matched with what the latter detects.
